targets.from: judgement values, no photographs measured: an erect, much-branched dense shrub about as wide as tall (FEIS)

young.note: a small dense bush on a sunny ridge or a seedling on a stump in the redwoods

old.note: a tall, rangy old shrub in redwood shade, spindly and open below

description: A dense evergreen shrub of the redwood understory and the brushy coastal ridges, with small, stiff, shiny dark leaves along its many stems. Its sweet, small black berries ripen in late summer and fall.

season_notes.winter: Glossy dark green in the forest shade, the berries mostly gone.
season_notes.spring: Bronze-red new shoots and clusters of tiny pink bells.
season_notes.summer: Green berries swell along the stems.
season_notes.fall: Heavy with shiny black berries that bears, foxes and birds come for.

range.where: redwood and Douglas-fir forest and coastal ridges from British Columbia to the Santa Cruz Mountains; Marin, the Peninsula and San Francisco's north slopes

notes: Grown from coffeeberry, another evergreen shrub of the forest edge with berries, but with smaller (2-5 cm), darker, glossier leaves, a more upright, narrower shape (W/H 1.0 against coffeeberry's 1.4) and reddish young stems. Spring is warmer in hue for the bronze-red new growth, and the palette adds a red-bronze entry. FEIS: generally 0.5-4.6 m, spindly and sprawling in deep shade and dwarfed to about 1-1.5 m on sunny cutover ground; flowers pink to white bells March to May in California; berries shiny purple-black, July to October. Berry eaters from FEIS (bears, foxes, squirrels, towhees, thrushes); deer browse is rated fair to poor but steady through the year. Cannot express: its habit of sprouting from old redwood stumps and logs.
